$description: CoForge design tokens. Sourced from @carbon/themes 11.79.0 (Apache-2.0), which publishes W3C DTCG natively — no conversion was needed. ADR-001: the repository authors v0; after the inversion point Figma owns tokens and this file mirrors.

coforge.note: Semantic tokens reference the palette by alias, exactly as Carbon ships them. Aliases are preserved rather than resolved so re-theming stays possible.

brand_primitives_added.what: palette.bone, palette.ink, palette.coral (.default + .text) — CoForge's own primitives, added alongside the Carbon mirror, never inside it (ADR-011).
brand_primitives_added.not_imported: ART-005's coherent ramps (taupe, neutral) are NOT imported step-for-step — only their evidenced single-step endpoints (bone, ink) exist in any artifact this agent may read. See validation/apply-brand-colour-layer.py's OPEN QUESTIONS output.
brand_primitives_added.gate: Gate A — suggest-only, pending human approval

ai.$description: One-off AI-surface values Carbon never ramped. They exist here because Carbon's own white.json and g100.json break its alias convention and inline these four as literals in the semantic layer. Hoisted to the primitive layer so the contract holds: exactly one layer carries numbers, everything above it aliases.

caret-bottom-background-dark.$description: AI popover caret bottom background, dark

caret-bottom-background-actions-dark.$description: AI popover caret bottom action background, dark

caret-bottom-background-actions.$description: AI popover caret bottom background for actions

default-a00.$description: black.default at 0 alpha. MINTED 2026-09-01 to repair C-021 — Carbon's alpha was transcribed into an extension and applied by nothing, leaving 53 semantic tokens fully opaque since the first token commit. DTCG has no alias-with-modifier, and the semantic layer may hold no literals, so the alpha has to live on a primitive. hex carries the alpha byte: a 6-digit hex beside an alpha field contradicts itself, and two consumers here read hex and never look at alpha.

coforge.intentional_duplicate: Shares #e8e8e8 with palette.white.Hover. Inherited from Carbon, not authored here. Left as two names deliberately: gray.10Hover is the hover state of the gray ramp's 10 step, white.Hover is the hover state of the white surface. They coincide at one value today and are free to diverge upstream. Collapsing them would couple two independent Carbon concepts and make a future Carbon release silently unmergeable.

default.$description: CoForge coral — accent and CONTAINER role only. Fills shapes, large-type CTAs, the wordmark C. NEVER body text, small labels, captions, legends, table values or form hints, on any ground (brand.md §3 binding rule) — measures 2.82:1 on bone / 3.33:1 on white, below the 4.5:1 AA text floor at every size this brand permits for small text.

coforge.origin: CoForge brand primitive — not sourced from @carbon/themes
coforge.evidence: brand.md §3 ('There is exactly one hot accent... coral'); ART-005 § Brand signal worth carrying, § Contrast.
coforge.gate: Gate A — suggested by token-keeper; not counted until a human approves (CLAUDE.md Gate table)

text.$description: CoForge coral, TEXT-SAFE role. The only coral value permitted to carry text, per brand.md §3's binding rule that the container coral and the text coral are two separate roles, not one colour used twice. Resolves OQ-6.

text.$description: The brand accent's TEXT-SAFE role — the only coral value permitted to carry text on bone (brand.md §3). GROUND-DEPENDENT (OQ-5): on dark, {coral.text} (#b03822) measures 2.95:1 against semantic-dark.background and fails, while {coral.default} (#f15b40) measures 5.43:1 there and passes — so the dark alias is deliberately NOT the same primitive as light's. coforge.complete_scale: A complete imported ladder. A layout consumes steps directly by name, so most steps are never aliased by a semantic token and that is the scale working as intended — unlike colour, spacing has no role layer between the primitive and the surface.

spacing.$description: Structural spacing scale. Transcribed from @carbon/layout 11.58.0 (Apache-2.0) — no brand signal opposes a different cadence (token-axes-proposal.md §2). 13 steps; component-index.json's spacing-scale component currently was extended to 13 on 2026-08-28; the contract is exact. script imports faithfully and flags, not resolves.

typography.$description: Typography primitives + semantic scale. AUTHORED per brand.md §4 (OQ-2 resolved: Anek Latin). Not a Carbon import — see this script's module docstring for the per-field provenance breakdown.

size.$description: Curated stopping points, not Carbon's 23-step compiled-formula ramp (brand.md §4: one scale, used at two densities, not a long undifferentiated ramp). AUTHORED.

03.$description: 16px — body. The tracking curve's zero-crossing lives near here.

weight.$description: light/regular/semibold transcribed from @carbon/type 11.66.0's compiled fontWeights export. heavy/black are CoForge-authored — Carbon's ceiling is 600; brand.md §4 evidences a 700 display weight and requires weight, not size, to carry hierarchy.

coforge.complete_scale: An authored range, not a used-subset. brand.md §4 makes weight the primary carrier of hierarchy, so the range has to exist before every rung is spent — a scale that only contains what today's eight levels happen to use cannot absorb a ninth without a token change. light (300) and black (800) are currently unaliased and that is the intended state; Anek Latin serves the full 100-800 range.

heavy.$description: AUTHORED. Evidenced display weight [ART-005 § Type] — "set at heavy weight (700)". Carbon has no value here.

black.$description: AUTHORED headroom, not currently used by any typography.scale level. Anek Latin serves weights to 800 (brand.md §4); reserved for a future display need.

tracking.$description: A curve, not a constant (brand.md §4). Paired 1:1 by index with typography.size — tightens as size grows. Only step 07 is evidenced; steps 01-06 are AUTHORED interpolation and NEED VISUAL TESTING before being treated as final.

01.$description: AUTHORED interpolation — slightly open at small size, per brand.md §4's "relaxes to normal or slightly open at small sizes." NOT evidenced. Needs visual testing.

02.$description: AUTHORED interpolation. NOT evidenced. Needs visual testing.

03.$description: AUTHORED interpolation — the curve's zero-crossing, placed at body size deliberately earlier than Carbon's own table (which stays at 0 until ~92px; proposal §3). NOT evidenced. Needs visual testing.

04.$description: AUTHORED interpolation. NOT evidenced. Needs visual testing.

05.$description: AUTHORED interpolation. NOT evidenced. Needs visual testing.

06.$description: AUTHORED interpolation. NOT evidenced. Needs visual testing.

07.$description: EVIDENCED [ART-005 § Type] — "-0.125rem (-2px) tracking at 62px." The only evidenced point on this curve; every other step is this script's interpolation toward it.

family.$description: AUTHORED per brand.md §4 (OQ-2 resolved 2026-08-27: Anek Latin; mono added 2026-08-28). Two primitives, because there are two actual typefaces. There is deliberately no display/body split here: 'display' and 'body' are ROLES, and roles live at the semantic layer where typography.scale.* already expresses them by which level draws which family. Carrying the role down into the primitive layer produced two leaves holding a byte-identical stack — a value reachable by two names, which is the same defect CoForge refused to inherit from coforge.com. If display and body ever diverge, add a third primitive and repoint the affected scale levels; the levels are where that decision belongs.

sans.$description: Anek Latin. Every non-code level: display, h1, h2, h3, body, body-sm, caption. CoForge is single-family for prose (brand.md §4).

mono.$description: Code and token values. Source Code Pro, selected on measurement [ART-007 § Optical pairing] — its x-height ratio is 0.486 against Anek Latin's 0.488, a 0.4% difference. Inline code sits inside body text, so a mismatched x-height reads as a size change mid-sentence and invites a compensating size nudge that then breaks alignment in tables. The nearest rival was 14x further off. Not a brand gesture — a face chosen to be unnoticeable next to the one that is.

scale.$description: AUTHORED. The only 8 names component-index.json's type-scale component declares. Composite $type 'typography' — every field inside $value is an alias string, never a literal. Every level carries the tabular-figures extension (see family/$description above and each level's $extensions).

display.$description: Stage register hero / key figures. Evidenced size and tracking [ART-005 § Type].

coforge.reason: Anek Latin's digits are proportional by default — a '1' measures 7.7% narrower than a '0' [ART-006 § The finding that decides it]. DTCG has no font-variant-numeric $type, so this is carried as an extension. Binding per brand.md §4: tabular figures are not a per-screen choice — anything consuming this scale level MUST apply font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; proportional figures are the exception a designer must ask for.
coforge.figma_exclusion_reason: A composite of family, size, weight and tracking. Figma expresses this as a TEXT STYLE, which can itself bind each of its fields to the size/, weight/, tracking/ and family/ variables that DO import. The composite is not lost — it is materialised as the Figma primitive that actually models it.

elevation.$description: Elevation geometry (authored) + the existing shadow colour (aliased, not duplicated). See build_elevation() docstring notes in this script for the visual-confirmation flag.

shadow.$description: Geometry AUTHORED (nothing exists upstream to import — Carbon ships zero DTCG shadow tokens; the only artefact is one line of hardcoded Sass). Colour ALIASED from the existing, correct semantic.shadow — not duplicated. brand.md §2: a single soft shadow, never more than one depth — hence exactly two states.

none.$description: No shadow — DTCG's documented way to express zero shadow layers. Used by flat surfaces.

coforge.figma_exclusion_reason: A composite of colour, offset, blur and spread — and DTCG allows a list of layers, which is how elevation.shadow.none expresses zero shadow as []. Figma models this as an EFFECT STYLE. Imported as a variable it collapses to FLOAT 0, which is indistinguishable from a real zero.

raised.$description: Single soft shadow (brand.md §2 — never more than one depth at a time). Geometry (2px/6px) is Carbon's own number (@carbon/styles box-shadow mixin) used as a STARTING POINT, NOT AN IMPORT — no such token exists upstream. NEEDS VISUAL CONFIRMATION against the brand's warmer, softer language before being treated as final. coforge.note: Non-standard DTCG $type — an array of pure alias strings, the same documented-extension shape Carbon itself uses for its own 'transition' $type. Not a DTCG-spec type.
coforge.figma_exclusion_reason: Not a value at all — a CONSTRAINT naming which typography.scale levels a density register is permitted to draw from. cf-type-scale declares all 8 levels; stage permits 5 and document 6, so the constraint carries real information held nowhere else. But a constraint is not a thing a designer picks from a variable picker. It belongs beside the component contract's variants, and is consumed in code.
